mcgowan_final.label: intermediate
mcgowan_final.note: McGowan grade II (intermediate) from stage 2 onward: objective sensory loss and intrinsic weakness are on record and no interosseous muscle is paralysed. The Goldberg et al. subdivision of grade II (IIA/IIB by extent of motor deficit, recorded in C34) is NOT implemented — the consulted reproduction gives the split's existence, not mechanically applicable sub-criteria, so the block grades II and says so.

mcgowan_stage1.note: Not yet classifiable at stage 1: the grade turns on the motor examination (weakness separates I from II; paralysis separates II from III), and no motor finding is on record until the stage-2 battery. The block's pending state is the honest one — a severity grade is not a history product.

criteria_comparison.note: The McGowan grade and the board are different instruments and the case keeps them separate: the grade states SEVERITY (how much nerve), the board states SITE (which level). A grade II lesion can sit at the elbow or the wrist; grading this patient II at stage 2 did not localize him, and the case's adjudication never asks it to. Where case 4's CTS-6 both diagnosed and graded, this case's instrument only grades — the localization is carried by the branch anatomy and the electrodiagnostic protocol.

adjudication.diagnosis_label: Ulnar neuropathy at the elbow (cubital tunnel syndrome), right — McGowan grade II (intermediate); localized by the dorsal cutaneous branch pattern, a positive Tinel at the elbow, an enlarged nerve at the medial epicondyle on ultrasound, and an electrodiagnostic protocol meeting the practice parameter's focal-lesion criteria with inching localization across the elbow. The wrist hypothesis that framed the patient's own account is excluded anatomically at stage 2 and retired on the board at stage 3.

evidence_chain.criterion: Branch anatomy — the dorsal ulnar cutaneous branch
evidence_chain.role: The case's decisive examination finding. The dorsal cutaneous branch leaves the ulnar nerve in the forearm, proximal to the wrist, and supplies the dorsal medial hand and the dorsal medial one and a half fingers (major.ulnar, C30). A lesion inside Guyon's canal cannot touch it — the linked clinical record states the wrist pattern verbatim: in a wrist lesion the dorsal cutaneous branch is spared and sensory loss is confined to the palmar medial one and a half fingers. This patient's dorsal territory is involved, so an isolated wrist lesion is anatomically excluded from stage 2, whatever the exposure history suggests. The finding carries no likelihood ratio — no consulted source gives an accuracy pair for it — and needs none: its force is anatomical, not statistical.

evidence_chain.criterion: Examination likelihood ratio — Tinel's sign at the elbow
evidence_chain.role: Percussion over the cubital tunnel reproduces the distal paresthesias. LR+ 35.0, computed from the consulted pair (C33): sensitivity 0.70 from the primary study's own count (31 of 44 extremities with electrodiagnostically proven cubital tunnel syndrome, Novak et al. 1994) and specificity 0.98 as tabulated in the consulted evidence summary. The board moves 0.22 -> 0.9080 at stage 2 and retires C8 radiculopathy, plexopathy and neurogenic thoracic outlet syndrome. The spectrum caveat is part of the entry: Novak's controls were asymptomatic volunteers, so the pair measures separation from health, not from this differential — the number is entered as computed from the cited pair, with the caveat stated, and the case's localization does not rest on it alone (the dorsal finding and the electrodiagnosis are independent legs).

Flexor carpi ulnaris and the medial half of flexor digitorum profundus are weak (4/5). Their branches leave the nerve in the forearm, proximal to the wrist: a Guyon's canal lesion cannot weaken them. Together with the dorsal sensory finding this is the second anatomical leg against the wrist hypothesis — the wrist pattern in the linked record is intrinsic hand muscles only (C30). No likelihood ratio is entered; the consulted sources give no accuracy pair for the pattern, and the case does not invent one.

Ulnar nerve cross-sectional area 14 mm2 at the medial epicondyle, above the 10 mm2 cutoff of the consulted meta-analysis (C32). LR+ 9.4444 computed from its pooled pair at that cutoff (sensitivity 0.85, specificity 0.91). The board moves 0.9080 -> 0.9894 at stage 3, retiring the wrist hypothesis (0.0024) and the residual. The wrist ultrasound the learner ordered first found a normal canal and no mass — true, and non-contributory: the lesion was never there to be found.

evidence_chain.criterion: Electrodiagnostic protocol — the practice parameter's criteria
evidence_chain.role: The across-elbow motor study meets the AAEM practice parameter's focal-lesion criteria (C31): absolute across-elbow velocity 38 m/s (criterion: below 50 m/s), 18 m/s slower than the below-elbow-to-wrist segment (criterion: more than 10 m/s slower), and a 28% CMAP amplitude drop across the segment (criterion: greater than 20%). LR+ 7.4 computed at the least favourable combination the parameter's review supports (sensitivities 37-86%, specificities 95% or greater across its 13 qualifying studies) — a disclosed floor, the same construction case 4 applied to its parameter. The board closes at 0.9986. Inching localizes the maximal change to the segment at the medial epicondyle (f.edx-inching-localization).

The protocol's extension legs do the excluding the parameter prescribes (C31): the medial antebrachial cutaneous SNAP — a medial cord / lower trunk sensory branch that never travels in the ulnar nerve — is normal, against plexopathy and neurogenic thoracic outlet syndrome; the dorsal ulnar cutaneous SNAP is abnormal, placing the lesion at or proximal to that branch's takeoff (f.duc-snap-abnormal); the ulnar sensory SNAP is reduced, a postganglionic pattern that a preganglionic C8 root lesion does not produce (f.ulnar-snap-abnormal); and the needle examination finds chronic neurogenic change confined to ulnar muscles with non-ulnar C8 muscles and cervical paraspinals normal (f.needle-emg-pattern). The electrodiagnostic order is therefore classified safety-net for the plexopathy hypothesis even though its headline finding also carries the board's final LR — its designed role, per the parameter, is exclusion as much as confirmation.

excluded.basis: Excluded anatomically before it is excluded statistically: (1) the dorsal ulnar cutaneous territory is involved (f.dorsal-ulnar-sensory-loss) — the branch arises proximal to the wrist and is spared in wrist lesions, the pattern the linked clinical record major.ulnar states verbatim (C30); (2) forearm muscles are weak (f.fcu-fdp-weakness) — a wrist lesion affects intrinsic hand muscles only; (3) Tinel's sign is at the elbow, not over the canal (f.tinel-elbow, f.tinel-guyon-absent), and combined pressure-flexion at the elbow reproduces the symptoms (f.pressure-flexion-positive); (4) the wrist ultrasound the learner ordered shows a normal canal with no ganglion or mass (f.wrist-us-normal); (5) the nerve is enlarged at the elbow, not the wrist (f.elbow-us-csa-enlarged, meas.elbow-ulnar-csa 14 mm2 against meas.wrist-ulnar-csa 5 mm2); (6) inching localizes the conduction change across the elbow (f.edx-inching-localization) and the dorsal cutaneous SNAP is abnormal (f.duc-snap-abnormal). Workbench posterior 0.0024, ruled out at stage 3. The cycling exposure is real and the canal is a real site — the case never claims Guyon's canal lesions do not happen to cyclists; it claims this patient's lesion is not one, on branch anatomy the learner's own examination elicited at stage 2.

Excluded by conjunction: (1) the sensory pattern is the ulnar nerve's territory, sharply bounded, not a C8 dermatome's wider and less bounded field, and there are no neck or proximal symptoms (f.no-neck-or-proximal-symptoms); (2) the ulnar sensory SNAP is reduced (f.ulnar-snap-abnormal) — a root lesion is preganglionic and leaves the SNAP intact, so a reduced SNAP places the lesion in the nerve, not the root; (3) the needle examination finds the abnormality confined to ulnar-innervated muscles with non-ulnar C8 muscles (extensor indicis, flexor pollicis longus) and cervical paraspinals normal (f.needle-emg-pattern) — the extension the practice parameter prescribes for exactly this exclusion (C31); (4) conduction localizes across the elbow (f.edx-across-elbow-slowing, f.edx-inching-localization). Workbench posterior 0.0165 at stage 2 (retired there by the Tinel weight) and 0.0003 at close.

Excluded by the medial antebrachial cutaneous evidence, twice: the territory is clinically intact (f.mabc-territory-intact) and its SNAP is normal (f.mabc-snap-normal). That nerve is a branch of the medial cord carrying lower-trunk fibres that never enter the ulnar nerve; a lower-trunk or medial-cord lesion sufficient to denervate ulnar intrinsics would be expected to involve it. The needle examination adds normal non-ulnar medial-cord muscles (f.needle-emg-pattern). Workbench posterior 0.0071, ruled out at stage 2.

Excluded on the same medial antebrachial cutaneous evidence as the plexopathy (f.mabc-territory-intact, f.mabc-snap-normal), with the clinical pattern against it throughout: no proximal pain, no whole-hand or exertional symptoms, a sharply ulnar picture in a nerve whose lesion is localized across the elbow by conduction (f.no-neck-or-proximal-symptoms, f.edx-inching-localization). Neurogenic thoracic outlet syndrome is the plexopathy's named mechanism in this differential, and the two fall together on the SNAP evidence. Workbench posterior 0.0083, ruled out at stage 2.

The residual retires arithmetically, as residuals do: it carries no finding of its own and is diluted below the rule-out line at stage 3 (0.0045) once the elbow ultrasound's likelihood ratio lands on the truth. Nothing in the presentation ever pointed at a named alternative the board lacks — no diffuse pattern (f.edx-no-diffuse-process), no median or radial involvement (f.no-other-territory-involvement).

available_tests.name: Targeted localization examination battery (sensory mapping by branch territory, ulnar motor examination, Froment and Wartenberg signs, Tinel at elbow and wrist, combined pressure-flexion, medial antebrachial cutaneous screen)
available_tests.note: The battery is classified discriminating, and the reason is its percussion member: Tinel's sign at the elbow carries the board's largest likelihood ratio (LR+ 35.0 computed, C33) and moves the lead by 0.688. But the battery's teaching member carries no number at all: the dorsal cutaneous sensory loss it elicits excludes the wrist hypothesis anatomically (C30) while the machinery, which can only weigh what sources quantify, records that exclusion in the adjudication rather than on the board. A battery whose decisive finding is unquantified is this case in miniature — the mirror of case 4, where the battery's decisive member was a quantified negative.

available_tests.name: Wrist ultrasound (ulnar nerve at Guyon's canal)
available_tests.note: The learner's first imaging order, bought by the cycling frame: it images the canal the anchor names. Its result is true — the canal is normal, there is no ganglion — and the machinery classifies it non-contributory: no likelihood ratio, no criteria input, no exclusion the anatomy had not already made at the same stage. It is case 4's cervical MRI in a different modality and at a different site: an order placed to confirm a prior, answered honestly, changing nothing.

available_tests.name: Elbow ultrasound (ulnar nerve cross-sectional area at the medial epicondyle)
available_tests.note: Ordered once the examination had localized clinically. Classified discriminating on the rule-out leg: its likelihood ratio (LR+ 9.4444 computed, C32) carries the wrist hypothesis and the residual across the rule-out line at stage 3 — the stage the learner's anchor is scored at, because this is the result the learner read and still held the wrist at 0.16.

available_tests.name: Electrodiagnostic protocol for ulnar neuropathy at the elbow (AAEM practice parameter: across-elbow motor conduction, inching, ulnar and dorsal ulnar cutaneous sensory studies, medial antebrachial cutaneous SNAP, needle extension to non-ulnar C8 / medial-cord muscles and cervical paraspinals, contralateral and non-ulnar nerve screen)
available_tests.note: The parameter's protocol (C31), ordered whole. Its headline finding carries the board's final likelihood ratio (LR+ 7.4 computed at the parameter's least favourable supported combination), yet the machinery classifies the order safety-net: by stage 4 the lead moves only 0.0092 and every rival is already retired, so the order's discriminating work is nil and its real work is the exclusion set the parameter designs it for — plexopathy declared as the must-not-miss, with radiculopathy and diffuse neuropathy excluded by the same legs. A confirmation instrument arriving after the board has converged is scored for what it still does, not for what it would have done earlier.

inputs.label: Paresthesia in the ulnar distribution (sensory symptoms)
Objective sensory loss on examination in ulnar territory (dorsal and/or palmar)
Detectable motor weakness in ulnar-innervated muscles
Paralysis of one or more interosseous muscles

criteria_blocks.label: McGowan grading of ulnar nerve compression (McGowan 1950)
criteria_blocks.note: The three grades as the consulted reproduction states them (C34): grade I (minimal) — sensory symptoms without detectable intrinsic weakness; grade II (intermediate) — weakness and some wasting of the interossei; grade III (severe) — paralysis of one or more interossei with wasting. Goldberg et al. (1989) subdivided grade II into IIA/IIB by extent of motor deficit; the consulted reproduction records the subdivision's existence but not mechanically applicable sub-criteria, so the block does not implement it and says so. The grade is a severity statement, not a localization: it is evaluated at every stage and never enters the board.
criteria_blocks.pending_label: not yet classifiable — the motor examination that separates the grades is not yet on record
criteria_blocks.system: McGowan grading (McGowan 1950) — three severity grades of ulnar nerve compression at the elbow, mechanically evaluated from the staged examination

findings.text: Numbness and tingling in the little finger and the ulnar half of the ring finger of the right hand, six months, gradually worsening; the thumb, index and middle fingers have never been involved (case data).

The paresthesias are worst at night and on waking, and are provoked by sustained elbow flexion — driving, holding a phone to the ear, sleeping with the elbow bent (case data). A symptom pattern that points at the elbow segment, present in the history from the first stage; the learner's wrist framing never engages it.

He rides a road bicycle with drop handlebars at weekends, two to four hours at a time, and notices the tingling after long rides (case data). The exposure is real — sustained weight-bearing through the hypothenar heel of the hand loads Guyon's canal — and it is the instalment of the case's anchor: a true exposure history, attached by the patient and then the learner to the wrong lesion.

He drives long-distance freight for a living and rests his right elbow on the cab door frame for hours at a stretch, elbow flexed (case data). The counter-exposure, also present from stage 1: prolonged flexion and direct pressure at the cubital tunnel. The case records both exposure stories without asserting causation for either — occupation and pastime are history, and the localization is made on anatomy and instruments, not on which story is told first.

An intermittent ache at the medial side of the right elbow, worse after long drives (case data). Nonspecific, recorded because a localization case should record the symptom that sits at the true level even when it proves nothing alone.

Clumsiness of the right hand: he drops keys, fumbles buttons, and his grip on the gear lever feels unreliable (case data). Subjective motor involvement — the symptom that will make the McGowan grade turn on the stage-2 motor examination.

No neck pain, no shoulder or proximal arm pain, no symptoms outside the ulnar digits, no exertional arm symptoms and no colour or temperature change in the hand (case data). A recorded absence of the proximal story: the C8, plexopathy and thoracic-outlet hypotheses are carried on dermatomal and neuroanatomical overlap, not on any proximal symptom this patient reports.

Diminished light touch and pinprick over the dorsal medial hand and the dorsal surfaces of the little finger and the ulnar half of the ring finger, right (case data) — the territory of the dorsal cutaneous branch of the ulnar nerve. That branch leaves the nerve in the forearm, proximal to the wrist, and the linked clinical record states the consequence verbatim: in a lesion at the wrist the dorsal cutaneous branch is spared and sensory loss is confined to the palmar medial one and a half fingers (major.ulnar, C30). Its involvement here excludes an isolated Guyon's canal lesion on anatomy. No likelihood ratio is entered: no consulted source gives an accuracy pair for this sign, and the case does not invent one — its force is that a wrist lesion cannot produce it at all.

Diminished light touch and pinprick over the palmar surfaces of the little finger and the ulnar half of the ring finger and the medial palm, right (case data) — the territories of the superficial branch and the palmar cutaneous branch (major.ulnar, C30). Expected at either level; it is the dorsal finding, not this one, that localizes.

Weakness of flexor carpi ulnaris (wrist flexion deviates radially; 4/5) and of flexor digitorum profundus to the ring and little fingers (4/5), right (case data). Both muscles are supplied by branches the ulnar nerve gives off in the forearm, proximal to the wrist (major.ulnar, C30) — the record's wrist pattern is intrinsic hand muscles only, so forearm weakness is the second anatomical leg against the wrist hypothesis. The muscles' own records resolve their innervation to the ulnar nerve records (the flexor digitorum profundus phrase is partial in the Milestone 35 pass — its medial half resolves to the ulnar nerve, its lateral half's anterior interosseous branch is absent from the Body Model; C30).

Weakness of the intrinsic hand muscles, right: finger abduction and adduction 4/5, first dorsal interosseous 4/5, abductor digiti minimi 4/5, thumb adduction 4/5 (case data). Expected at either ulnar level — the intrinsics are the hand's ulnar muscles in both patterns (major.ulnar, C30) — so this finding grades severity (it is a McGowan input) without localizing. Honesty note, mirroring case 4's thenar finding: these muscles' clinical records name their innervation as the deep branch of the ulnar nerve, and the Milestone 35 pass records that phrase UNRESOLVED — no FMA class carries the branch's name and no inventory record exists for it (C30) — so this finding links the ulnar trunk records and the muscle records, and says so, rather than implying a branch record the Body Model does not hold.

Froment's sign positive, right: holding a sheet of paper between thumb and index against a pull, the thumb's interphalangeal joint flexes to compensate for the weak adductor pollicis (case data) — the test as the linked clinical record describes it (major.ulnar, C30). An intrinsic-weakness sign: it confirms ulnar motor involvement and, like the weakness itself, does not localize the level.

Wartenberg's sign present, right: the little finger rests abducted from the ring finger at rest and cannot be adducted to it (case data) — palmar interosseous weakness, the adduction counterpart of the abduction weakness above. Non-localizing, recorded as part of the intrinsic picture.

Visible guttering of the first dorsal interosseous space and early flattening of the hypothenar eminence, right (case data) — early wasting of the intrinsic muscles, the finding that, with weakness and without paralysis, places the patient in McGowan's intermediate grade rather than the minimal one (C34).

Early ulnar claw posture of the ring and little fingers on attempted extension, right: metacarpophalangeal hyperextension with interphalangeal flexion, mild (case data) — the posture the HPO class HP:0001178 describes as associated with lesions of the ulnar nerve (C11). Recorded as part of the intrinsic-loss picture; it is not a McGowan input in the consulted reproduction and the block does not use it.

ABSENT finding, recorded explicitly: no interosseous muscle is paralysed — every affected muscle retains antigravity movement at 4/5 (case data). The examined absence is what keeps this patient out of McGowan grade III, whose criterion is paralysis of one or more interossei (C34), and it is recorded as an absence rather than left as missing data — the same discipline as case 4's thenar finding.

lr.note: LR+ 35.0, computed from the consulted pair (C33): sensitivity 0.70 — the primary study's own count, Tinel's sign present in 31 of 44 extremities with electrodiagnostically proven cubital tunnel syndrome (Novak et al. 1994) — and specificity 0.98 as tabulated for the sign in cubital tunnel syndrome in the consulted evidence summary (Physio-pedia). 0.70 / (1 - 0.98) = 35.0. Spectrum caveat, stated rather than buried: the primary study's controls were asymptomatic volunteers, so the pair measures separation from health, not from this case's live differential (a wrist lesion, a root lesion), and the true discriminating weight against those rivals is certainly smaller. The value is entered exactly as the cited pair computes it, the caveat travels with it, and the adjudication's localization rests on three further legs (dorsal branch anatomy, forearm motor pattern, electrodiagnostic localization) that do not depend on it.

findings.text: Tinel's sign at the elbow, right: percussion over the ulnar nerve behind the medial epicondyle reproduces tingling into the little finger and ulnar half of the ring finger (case data). A localizing sign by construction — percussion speaks at the level percussed — and the board's largest single weight (LR+ 35.0 computed, C33, with its spectrum caveat stated in the entry).

ABSENT finding, recorded explicitly: percussion over Guyon's canal at the wrist does not reproduce the symptoms (case data). The negative counterpart of the elbow sign — the percussion map points at one level only. No likelihood ratio is entered for the absence; no consulted source quantifies it.

Combined pressure-flexion test at the elbow positive, right: direct pressure over the cubital tunnel with the elbow held in full flexion reproduces the paresthesias within 30 seconds (case data). In the consulted primary study this combined manoeuvre was the most sensitive provocative test at 30 seconds (sensitivity 0.91, Novak et al. 1994, C33); its specificity is not stated in the consulted report, so no likelihood ratio is computed from it — it acts qualitatively, as corroboration at the elbow level, and the case says why it carries no number.

Sensation intact over the medial forearm, right — the territory of the medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve (case data). That nerve branches from the medial cord and carries lower-trunk fibres that never travel in the ulnar nerve: its sparing is the clinical half of the argument against a lower-trunk or medial-cord lesion, and its SNAP is the electrodiagnostic half (f.mabc-snap-normal). No likelihood ratio — no consulted source quantifies the sign.

Median and radial territories normal on examination, right: thenar strength and sensation full, wrist and finger extension full, no sensory loss outside the ulnar distribution (case data). The lesion's picture is one nerve's; a plexus process wide enough to denervate the ulnar intrinsics would not be expected to leave the rest of the hand this clean, and a diffuse neuropathy would not be unilateral and single-nerve.

Wrist ultrasound, right: the ulnar nerve at Guyon's canal is of normal calibre (meas.wrist-ulnar-csa) and the canal contains no ganglion, mass or anomalous muscle (case data). A true negative at the site the anchor names — and non-contributory in the machinery's classification, because by the time it resulted, the same stage's examination had already excluded a wrist lesion on branch anatomy. Negative imaging of the wrong site is not evidence about the right one.

lr.note: LR+ 9.4444, computed from the Chang et al. meta-analysis pair (C32): pooled sensitivity 0.85 and specificity 0.91 at the 10 mm2 cross-sectional-area cutoff (five studies pooled for the cutoff analysis; fourteen trials in the review). 0.85 / (1 - 0.91) = 9.4444. The pooling spans case-control studies whose non-case arms are largely participants without cubital tunnel syndrome rather than patients with this differential; the heterogeneity is inherited and labelled, as case 4 labelled its ultrasound pair's.

findings.text: Elbow ultrasound, right: ulnar nerve cross-sectional area 14 mm2 at the level of the medial epicondyle (meas.elbow-ulnar-csa) — enlarged against the 10 mm2 cutoff of the consulted meta-analysis, which reports the largest case-control calibre difference at the medial epicondyle level (C32). The swelling is at the elbow; the wrist measurement from the same workup is 5 mm2 (meas.wrist-ulnar-csa). An enlarged segment is a lesion's address, and this one's address is the cubital tunnel.

lr.note: LR+ 7.4, computed AT the least favourable combination the AAEM practice parameter's review supports (C31): sensitivities of electrodiagnostic studies for ulnar neuropathy at the elbow ranged from 37% to 86% across the parameter's 13 qualifying studies, with specificities of 95% or greater — 0.37 / (1 - 0.95) = 7.4. Because both figures are ranges, 7.4 is a FLOOR for the parameter's LR+, used as the point value with the direction of the approximation disclosed — the construction case 4 applied to its own practice parameter (C25). The heterogeneity behind the range (differing techniques and criteria across 1983-1996 studies) is the reason for the floor's conservatism, and is stated rather than smoothed.

findings.text: Electrodiagnostic protocol (AAEM practice parameter technique, C31: elbow in moderate flexion, 10 cm across-elbow distance, surface stimulation and recording): ulnar motor conduction across the elbow meets the parameter's focal-lesion criteria — the absolute across-elbow velocity is 38 m/s (criterion: less than 50 m/s; meas.ae-be-motor-cv), the across-elbow segment is 18 m/s slower than the below-elbow-to-wrist segment (criterion: more than 10 m/s slower; meas.be-w-motor-cv 56 m/s), and the CMAP negative-peak amplitude falls 28% across the segment (criterion: a decrease greater than 20%, conduction block / temporal dispersion of a focal demyelinating lesion; meas.cmap-amplitude-drop-pct). Three of the parameter's listed criteria are met together — the parameter itself notes that multiple internally consistent abnormalities are more convincing than isolated ones.

Inching study (the practice parameter's listed option, C31): stimulation in 1 cm increments across the elbow localizes the maximal latency and amplitude change to the segment at and immediately behind the medial epicondyle — the retrocondylar / cubital tunnel segment (case data). No likelihood ratio exists for inching in any source this case consulted; it is the protocol's localizer, and its verdict is a place, not a probability.

Dorsal ulnar cutaneous sensory nerve action potential reduced in amplitude, right (case data) — the electrodiagnostic twin of the stage-2 dorsal sensory finding. The branch leaves the nerve in the distal forearm; its involvement places the lesion at or proximal to the takeoff and is incompatible with an isolated Guyon's canal lesion, in the sensory fibre population this time. Qualitative, as the examination finding was: no consulted source gives an accuracy pair for it.

Medial antebrachial cutaneous sensory nerve action potential normal, right (case data). The nerve is a medial-cord branch carrying lower-trunk fibres and never travels with the ulnar nerve; a postganglionic lower-trunk or medial-cord lesion of this severity would be expected to reduce it. Its normality is the electrodiagnostic half of the plexopathy / thoracic-outlet exclusion, paired with the intact clinical territory (f.mabc-territory-intact). Qualitative — the parameter prescribes the extension studies without publishing per-branch accuracy pairs (C31).

Ulnar sensory nerve action potential (digit 5) reduced in amplitude, right (case data). A sensory axon-loss pattern distal to the dorsal root ganglion — postganglionic. A C8 root lesion sits proximal to the ganglion and leaves the SNAP intact; a reduced ulnar SNAP therefore places the sensory lesion in the nerve or plexus, not the root, and is the electrodiagnostic leg of the radiculopathy exclusion. Qualitative; no consulted source quantifies the pattern's accuracy as a standalone finding.

Needle examination, right: chronic neurogenic change (reduced recruitment, enlarged motor unit potentials) in first dorsal interosseous, abductor digiti minimi, flexor carpi ulnaris and flexor digitorum profundus IV; normal in non-ulnar C8 muscles (extensor indicis, flexor pollicis longus), in median lower-trunk muscles (abductor pollicis brevis), and in the cervical paraspinals (case data) — the extension the practice parameter prescribes when ulnar-innervated muscles are abnormal: non-ulnar C8 / medial cord / lower trunk muscles to exclude brachial plexopathy, and the cervical paraspinals to exclude radiculopathy (C31). The abnormality's map is one nerve's proximal-to-wrist span, and no other's.

Median and radial conduction studies normal bilaterally, and the contralateral (left) ulnar study normal (case data): no electrodiagnostic evidence of a diffuse polyneuropathy or a second entrapment — the practice parameter's standing instruction, when ulnar studies are abnormal, to carry out further studies to exclude a diffuse process (C31). This patient has no diabetes (case data), and the electrical picture agrees with the history: one nerve, one level.

ground_truth.diagnosis: Ulnar neuropathy at the elbow (cubital tunnel syndrome), right, McGowan grade II (intermediate) — localized by branch anatomy (dorsal cutaneous involvement, forearm motor involvement), percussion at the elbow, segmental enlargement at the medial epicondyle, and a practice-parameter electrodiagnostic protocol with inching localization across the elbow; Guyon's canal, C8 radiculopathy, lower-trunk/medial-cord plexopathy and neurogenic thoracic outlet syndrome excluded on the stated legs.
ground_truth.engine_state: No physiology link is declared: the engine has no peripheral-nerve, entrapment or demyelination state, and no engine output would be evidence about this patient's ulnar nerve. Case 2 set the precedent — a decorative link to the resting baseline would claim a connection that does not exist, so none is made.

criteria_block.combination: One declared classification block (mcgowan) is computed from the findings at every stage; it is not combined with the board. The adjudication states what the grade does and does not say: it grades severity and never localizes (adjudication.criteria_comparison).

hypotheses.label: Ulnar neuropathy at the elbow (cubital tunnel syndrome)

prior.note: VERIFY-FLAGGED PLACEHOLDER, not a measurement: no consulted source gives a base rate for this presentation in a defined population, so the split is an authoring choice for the exercise, labelled as such wherever it appears. The largest single named share, reflecting that ulnar neuropathy at the elbow is the common entrapment at this nerve — the practice parameter calls ulnar neuropathy at the elbow a common mononeuropathy, second only to carpal tunnel syndrome in incidence (C31) — but held close to the wrist share because this patient's history genuinely argues both levels and no discriminating examination exists yet at stage 1.

hypotheses.label: Ulnar neuropathy at the wrist (Guyon's canal)
hypotheses.mondo_note: No Guyon's-canal-specific class exists in Mondo: in-session OLS searches for 'Guyon' and for 'ulnar tunnel syndrome' returned only the generic class ulnar neuropathy MONDO:0007006 (C10, Milestone 43 addendum), whose own description names the axilla, the cubital tunnel and Guyon's canal as the nerve's common injury sites. The generic class is used with this note rather than asserting a site-specific class Mondo does not carry — the refusal discipline of case 4's pronator hypothesis, applied to a too-general class instead of an absent one. The hypothesis's site specificity lives in its label and its evidence, not in a fabricated code.

prior.note: VERIFY-FLAGGED PLACEHOLDER, not a measurement: no consulted source gives a base rate for this presentation in a defined population, so the split is an authoring choice for the exercise, labelled as such wherever it appears. The second share, and deliberately close behind the elbow's: the cycling history is a genuine Guyon's canal exposure, the intrinsic picture fits a wrist lesion, and at stage 1 nothing yet separates the levels. The hypothesis must be carried at full weight and retired by anatomy, not by dismissal — which is what makes the learner's later failure to retire it scorable.

hypotheses.label: C8 radiculopathy
hypotheses.mondo_note: No cervical-specific radiculopathy class exists in Mondo (C10, Milestone 41 addendum, re-used at Milestone 43). The generic radiculopathy class is used with this note rather than asserting a class Mondo does not carry — case 4's discipline, applied to the same hypothesis a level up the same limb.

imaging_assessment.atlas_contrast: The atlas Body Model DOES carry the structure: the Milestone 33 inventory records nerve.right-ulnar-nerve and nerve.left-ulnar-nerve, and the Milestone 39 clinical record major.ulnar built on them — and this case links those records. What the atlas has and the imaging lacks is the honest shape of this module's coverage, stated rather than smoothed.
imaging_assessment.statement: Neither shipped imaging series can show this case's structure, on two independent grounds, both re-verified by the checker at every run: (1) LABEL SET — the TotalSegmentator v1.0 label set is identical for the two subjects (104 labels each) and contains no nerve label of any kind, and no ulnar or elbow label; (2) FIELD OF VIEW — both series are CT thorax-abdomen-pelvis studies, so neither the elbow nor the wrist is inside the imaged volume. Case 4 faced one absent structure at one site; this case's question spans two sites and both are outside the volume, so no imaging_link is declared and the generic imaging machinery is deliberately not invoked. The case's two ultrasounds are authored encounters (case data), exactly as case 4's ultrasound was.

management.alternatives_considered: A wrist-directed pathway (Guyon's canal exploration or cycling-ergonomics management alone) is the live alternative the learner's framing implies; it was not this case's disposition because the lesion is localized to the elbow by four independent legs, and treating the wrist would leave a grade II elbow lesion untouched. A watch-and-wait pathway without referral is the other alternative; six months of progression with objective weakness and early wasting (grade II, not I) puts the case outside it. Both alternatives are recorded so the disposition is a decision, not a default.
management.disposition: Ulnar neuropathy at the elbow (cubital tunnel syndrome), right, McGowan grade II, localized as the adjudication states. Referral to a hand / peripheral-nerve surgeon with the localization, the grade and the electrodiagnostic report; interim measures are the referring service's to direct. The workbench adjudicates the lesion's SITE and SEVERITY — the questions this case was built to ask — and records treatment as a referral decision rather than prescribing: no treatment guideline for cubital tunnel syndrome was consulted for this case, and the case does not borrow authority it did not consult.

handoff.basis: Electrodiagnostically confirmed ulnar neuropathy localized to the elbow (cubital tunnel syndrome), McGowan grade II, with six months of progression, objective weakness and early wasting: the disposition's referral is to a hand / peripheral-nerve surgeon for decompression of the ulnar nerve at the elbow. The case hands off to the Theatre's procedure proc.ulnar-decompression (Milestone 44), whose standard configuration is the in-situ open decompression; whether the nerve also needs the anterior transposition configuration is decided at the operation's own stability assessment, an intraoperative finding this case cannot make from the workbench. The disposition text above is unchanged from Milestone 43, including its record that no treatment guideline for cubital tunnel syndrome was consulted for this case: the handoff names the operation the referral seeks, and borrows no guideline authority the case did not consult.
handoff.note: The loop the master plan section 7 and design/07 describe: the case's disposition is the Theatre attempt's starting point. In the Theatre, this same ulnar nerve (major.ulnar, in proc.ulnar-decompression's structures register) is the structure the operation decompresses and the first structure its safety gate protects, and the medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve this case never had occasion to name is the gate's second protected structure. history: No diabetes mellitus, no thyroid disease, no prior elbow or wrist trauma or surgery, no cervical spine history (case data) — recorded explicitly because case 4's differential ran on diabetes and this one's must not: the diffuse-neuropathy pull is absent here by history and confirmed absent electrodiagnostically at stage 4.
Weekend road cyclist for nine years; drop handlebars, rides of two to four hours (case data).
He attributes the symptoms to the bicycle and has shortened his rides; his employer has offered him a cab with an armrest he has not yet taken up (case data) — the framing the learner adopts.
patient.occupation: long-distance freight driver (case data). His occupation and his pastime are both recorded as history — prolonged elbow flexion and pressure at work, sustained hand weight-bearing on the bicycle — and the case asserts causation for neither: the localization is made on branch anatomy and instruments, not on which exposure is blamed.

presentation_stages.narrative: A 58-year-old right-hand-dominant man presents with six months of numbness and tingling in the right little finger and the ulnar half of the ring finger, worse at night and with sustained elbow flexion — driving, holding a phone. He drops keys and fumbles buttons. He drives freight long-distance, resting his right elbow on the cab door frame for hours; at weekends he rides a road bicycle on drop handlebars and notices the tingling after long rides, and he is sure the bicycle is the cause. He has an intermittent ache at the medial elbow. No neck pain, no proximal symptoms, no diabetes. Vitals (case data): afebrile, heart rate 68/min, blood pressure 128/80 mmHg.
presentation_stages.title: History — six months of ulnar paresthesias, two exposure stories

presentation_stages.narrative: The targeted examination maps the lesion's pattern before any instrument is used. Sensory loss covers the palmar ulnar territory AND the dorsal medial hand — the dorsal cutaneous branch's territory, which a wrist lesion spares. Flexor carpi ulnaris and the medial flexor digitorum profundus are weak, alongside the intrinsic hand muscles, with Froment's and Wartenberg's signs, early interosseous wasting, an early claw posture, and no paralysis anywhere. Tinel's sign is at the elbow and not at the wrist; combined pressure-flexion at the elbow reproduces the symptoms in under 30 seconds; the medial forearm's sensation is intact and no other territory is involved. The wrist ultrasound the learner orders shows a normal Guyon's canal with no mass. Every element of the wrist hypothesis's expected pattern is contradicted by something the examiner's own hands found — and the learner, holding the cycling frame, records the dorsal finding as a soft sign and keeps the wrist second only to the elbow.
presentation_stages.title: Examination — the branch pattern contradicts the wrist; a wrist ultrasound agrees with the wrong site

presentation_stages.narrative: Elbow ultrasound: the ulnar nerve measures 14 mm2 in cross-section at the medial epicondyle — enlarged against the consulted meta-analysis's 10 mm2 cutoff — against 5 mm2 at the same patient's wrist. The swelling sits at the elbow. On the workbench board the wrist hypothesis and the residual cross the rule-out line at this stage; the learner reads the result, moves the elbow up, and still holds the wrist at 0.16 — the stage at which the machinery scores the case's single anchoring event.
presentation_stages.title: Elbow ultrasound — the nerve is enlarged at the epicondyle, not the wrist

presentation_stages.narrative: The practice-parameter electrodiagnostic protocol closes the localization and clears the proximal field. Across-elbow motor conduction is 38 m/s, 18 m/s slower than the forearm segment, with a 28% amplitude drop — three of the parameter's focal-lesion criteria together; inching places the change at the medial epicondyle. The dorsal ulnar cutaneous SNAP is abnormal, the medial antebrachial cutaneous SNAP is normal, the ulnar SNAP is reduced in a postganglionic pattern, and the needle map confines the abnormality to ulnar muscles with non-ulnar C8 muscles and paraspinals clean. The learner commits to the elbow, McGowan grade II, and concedes the wrist to 0.04.
presentation_stages.title: Electrodiagnosis — slowing localized across the elbow; the proximal rivals cleared by the instruments built to clear them

validity.note: Every quantitative clinical claim in this case traces to a source in cases/parameters.json consulted in-session (C30-C34 for this case). The McGowan grades are the published classification's own, as reproduced in the consulted summary (C34). Likelihood ratios are arithmetic on cited sensitivity/specificity pairs, each with its construction disclosed: the Tinel LR+ from the primary study's sensitivity count and the consulted summary's specificity, with the healthy-control spectrum caveat stated in the entry (C33); the ultrasound LR+ from the meta-analysis's pooled pair at its stated cutoff (C32); the electrodiagnostic LR+ computed at the practice parameter's least favourable supported combination and disclosed as a floor (C31). Findings for which no source gives an accuracy pair — the dorsal cutaneous pattern, the forearm motor pattern, the SNAP pattern — carry no likelihood ratio and act through the adjudication's stated anatomy, never through invented numbers.
